messages:
Maya G: Quick heads-up — I brought up HoloQuant-13B int4 on staging (staging-hq-2026-03-18). Short summary: ~2.8x token cost reduction vs fp16 but we’re seeing a non-trivial quality hit on the 'priming' slice. Details below.

Tom R: numbers?

Maya G: Scorecard (priming slice, n=1,024):
- fp16 baseline: EM 72.1, BLEU 65.0, p50 latency 180ms, token cost ~$0.024 per 1k tokens
- int4: EM 63.3, BLEU 59.2, p50 latency 140ms, token cost ~$0.0085 per 1k tokens
Bootstrap 95% CI for EM delta: [-13.1, -10.2] points.

Priya S: Oof. That EM drop is larger than I was hoping. Multi-turn?

Maya G: Multi-turn (n=512) shows smaller reg: EM -6.2, BLEU -4.8. Failure modes: omitted priming tokens, increased numeric hallucinations. Example snippet: 

Maya G: ```
prompt: "Given product history X, recommend next three features"
fp16: "1) autosave 2) shared drafts 3) analytics dashboard"
int4: "1) analytics dashboard 2) consider monitoring"  <-- missing/autosave/shuffled order
```

Oliver K: pattern sounds like reduced attention fidelity on long prefix. Any telemetry on KV cache evictions or kv-shape mismatch?

Maya G: KV cache patterns look normal; profiling shows quantized matmul noise spike on earlier layers for tokens > 512. Also SNR drop correlated with long priming (>800 tokens).

Tom R: How much of our prod traffic actually hits the long-priming slice? If it's small we can route.

Priya S: From sampling last week: ~12% of requests have priming > 700 tokens; but only 4% are product-critical flows (gtm/editor autosave).

Maya G: Econ quick calc: if we switch 100% traffic to int4 => ~2.8x cost reduction but overall product Q metric drops ~0.8% (weighted by slice prevalence). Hybrid routing: route short/low-risk requests to int4 and funnel long/critical to fp16 yields ~1.6x net cost reduction with <0.2% product Q delta.

Priya S: Sounds reasonable. Ops considerations? Canary plan? SLAs?

Tom R: My proposal:
- Canary 5% of traffic for 48h, split evenly across regions
- Monitor: priming EM, recall, latency p95, downstream error rate
- Automatic rollback trigger: EM delta <= -3 points on the priming slice for 30m window OR p95 latency > +20%

Maya G: +1. Also want to trial int6 (w/ optimized kernel) as a middle ground — expected ~1.7x cost reduction with <3pt EM drop based on sens tests. I'll run a quick microbench and post numbers by EOD.

Oliver K: Can we deploy per-route model flags in routing layer? E.g., /editor -> force fp16, /search -> allow int4.

Maya G: Yes, routing supports per-route model preferences. I'll add a default policy: short-text routes -> prefer int4; long-context routes -> prefer fp16; and a safety label for GTN product traffic to always use baseline.

ops-bot: deploy scheduled: hq-int4-canary -> 2026-03-20T22:00Z (notified #eng-deploy).

Priya S: Request: add the priming test set + eval harness to the GTN bucket and pin the baseline in the canary dashboard. I want automatic weekly regression checks.

Maya G: Will upload the priming test set and eval scripts to gs://redwood-evals/hq/priming/ and post link here once done. Also adding an eval alert: daily sample test, abort canary if EM delta < -3.

Tom R: Final ask for GTN/product: include a short guidance blurb in the rollout doc: "Hybrid routing recommended; do not route editor autosave traffic to int4 until int6/mitigation validated."

Maya G: Will draft that. TL;DR recs: 1) run int6 microbench; 2) canary int4 at 5% with rollback rules; 3) implement per-route overrides (editor=fp16); 4) add automated priming-slice checks to eval dashboard.

Priya S: Thanks — sounds like a pragmatic path. :thumbsup:

Maya G: Upload done: https://storage.redwood.ai/evals/hq/priming/2026-03-18 (scripts + sample outputs). I'll post the int6 numbers when ready.
